mainEntity.name: How much does a Hyundai i40 2.0 GDi engine replacement cost?

acceptedAnswer.text: A Hyundai i40 2.0 GDi (G4NC) engine replacement typically costs between £1,800 and £4,200 for the engine supply alone, depending on whether you choose used, reconditioned, or rebuilt. Supply and fit adds approximately £600-£1,000 in specialist labour. Dealer pricing can add 30-50% to these figures.

mainEntity.name: What are the signs of a failing G4NC engine in a Hyundai i40?

acceptedAnswer.text: Common warning signs that your Hyundai i40 2.0 GDi G4NC engine is failing include a flashing Check Engine light during acceleration, hesitation under load, rough idle, poor fuel economy, and cold-start timing chain rattle. Direct injection system issues can also cause hard starting and loss of power.

mainEntity.name: Is it worth replacing the engine in a Hyundai i40 2.0 GDi?

acceptedAnswer.text: This depends on the vehicle's value and condition. A typical Hyundai i40 2.0 GDi of relevant age is worth £3,000-£9,000. A rebuilt engine at £2,800-£4,200 may represent a significant portion of the vehicle's value. If the car is in good condition, well-maintained, and you intend to keep it for 2+ years, replacement is often worthwhile. If vehicle value is under £4,000, evaluate scrap value first.

mainEntity.name: What's the difference between the Hyundai i40 2.0 GDi and 1.7 CRDi engines?

acceptedAnswer.text: The main difference is fuel type and engine architecture: the 2.0 GDi is a petrol direct injection engine (G4NC) producing 177hp, while the 1.7 CRDi is a common-rail diesel (D4FD) with 116-141hp. The 1.7 CRDi has roughly 70-80% of replacement demand, but petrol GDi engines are simpler and often cheaper to replace.

mainEntity.name: Does the Hyundai i40 2.0 GDi have a timing belt or chain?

acceptedAnswer.text: The Hyundai i40 2.0 GDi (G4NC) has a timing chain, not a belt. This is a metal chain that should last the engine's lifetime, but timing chain tensioner wear has been reported on higher-mileage units. If you hear rattling on cold start, have the chain and tensioner inspected immediately.

mainEntity.name: How long does a Hyundai i40 2.0 GDi engine replacement take?

acceptedAnswer.text: A professional Hyundai i40 2.0 GDi engine replacement typically takes 1-3 working days. Specialist workshops can complete the job in 8-12 labour hours. Supply lead times vary: used engines 2-5 working days, reconditioned 5-10 working days, and rebuilt 7-14 working days. Confirm exact timelines with your chosen specialist.

historyTimeline.h2: Hyundai i40 2.0 GDi - Engine History & Specs at a Glance
historyTimeline.intro: The Hyundai i40 2.0 GDi was introduced in 2011 as the flagship petrol option in the i40 range, offering a 2.0-litre direct-injection four-cylinder engine. It remained in production through two generations until the i40 was discontinued in 2020.

milestones.description: G4NC, 2.0-litre GDi, 177hp - launched with the i40 VF generation
2015 - Original i40 generation with G4NC 177hp and 165hp variants
2020 - Facelift generation; G4NC continued with 177hp output alongside lower-output G4NA 2.0 MPI variants
End of i40 production; G4NC remains available through specialist suppliers

commonProblems.h2: Hyundai i40 2.0 GDi Engine Problems - Repair Cost vs Replacement
commonProblems.h3: The Hyundai i40 2.0 GDi G4NC is a generally reliable engine but has known weak points that can lead to significant repair costs. The direct injection system and timing chain require attention, and owners report issues with misfires and hesitation that often point to ignition or fuel system components. Rebuilt engines through EnginesMarket include upgraded components addressing the original failure point, plus a minimum 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty.

problems.h4: GDi Direct Injection System Failure - Why the Hyundai i40 2.0 GDi Loses Power and Misfires
problems.rootCause: High-pressure fuel pump wear, injector failure, or carbon build-up on intake valves - a common characteristic of direct injection petrol engines.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace HPFP and fuel rail components; system bleed and adaptation
repairOptions.longevity: Cost-effective fix if pump is the sole failure point

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace failed injectors; walnut shell intake valve cleaning if carbon build-up is present
repairOptions.longevity: Good mid-range option; extends engine life by 30,000+ miles

problems.vehicleValueCheck: A typical Hyundai i40 2.0 GDi of relevant age is worth approximately £3,000-£9,000 depending on mileage and condition. The replacement-to-value guidance is: - Vehicle worth under ~£5,000: repair or used engine typically makes more sense than a full rebuilt unit. - Vehicle worth ~£5,000-£8,000: evaluate both; reconditioned is viable if keeping the car 2+ years. - Vehicle worth ~£8,000-£15,000: reconditioned/rebuilt usually justifies the premium via warranty and reliability.
problems.recommendation: Investigate the fuel system and ignition components before committing to a full replacement. Many "engine failure" cases on the 2.0 GDi are actually high-pressure fuel pump, injector, or coil pack issues costing £400-£1,200 to fix - considerably less than a full engine replacement. However, if cylinder scoring from carbon debris is confirmed (as reported in owner forums), replacement becomes the only viable option.
